externalToolsHub.subtitle: MO2 · ComfyUI · Upscayl workflows plus setup-tool auto-connect

mo2.desc: The industry-standard mod manager for Fallout 4. Mossy reads your MO2 profile to understand your active mod list and load order. Install: Nexus Mod Manager page or official GitHub.

tips.0: Use separate MO2 profiles for different playthroughs or testing configurations.
tips.1: Enable "Manageable" mode in MO2 settings to allow Mossy to read your active plugin list.
tips.2: MO2 virtual file system (VFS) is transparent to the game — files in MO2 override order matches load order priority.
tips.3: Use the "Conflicts" tab in MO2 to see file-level asset conflicts before plugin-level conflicts.

comfyui.desc: Node-based AI image generation. Use for creating concept art, texture references, NPC portraits, and promotional artwork for your mods. Requires a GPU with at least 6 GB VRAM.

tips.0: Use ComfyUI's img2img workflow to generate texture variations from existing in-game screenshots.
tips.1: ControlNet pose conditioning helps create accurate character reference art matching FO4 skeleton proportions.
tips.2: Export AI-generated art at 4096x4096 minimum for texture use — then downscale and compress to DDS via the Textures & Materials hub.
tips.3: Stable Diffusion fine-tunes (LoRAs) trained on Fallout concept art can improve consistency of generated assets.

upscayl.desc: Free, open-source AI upscaler using Real-ESRGAN models. Ideal for upscaling low-res vanilla textures, reference photos, and UI elements before DDS conversion.

tips.0: Use RealESRGAN-x4plus for general texture upscaling. The result still needs compression to BC1/BC3/BC5/BC7 after upscaling.
tips.1: For face/portrait textures, use ESRGAN face models to preserve fine skin detail before re-exporting to FaceGen.
tips.2: Upscale vanilla 512x512 textures to 2048x2048 max — going higher than 4x the original yields diminishing returns for in-game use.
tips.3: After upscaling, always run through a normal map bake (xNormal or Substance Painter) to reconstruct lost surface detail as normals.

setupWizards.title: Run Setup Wizards
setupWizards.body: Detect F4SE, xEdit, MO2/Vortex, Creation Kit, and other tools. Mossy customizes her advice to what is actually installed.

modGoal.title: Pick a Modding Goal
modGoal.body: Open FO4 Mod Journey Hub → Roadmaps and generate a step-by-step plan. Whether you are adding weapons, quests, or worldspaces — start with a clear goal.

loadOrder.title: Know the Load Order Rules
loadOrder.body: Fallout 4 hard-caps at 254 standard ESM/ESP plugins (slot 0xFE is reserved for the ESL indicator). ESL-flagged plugins load in a separate FE000-FEFFF range and do not count toward that cap — each gets its own 2,048-FormID pool. Use FO4 Plugin & Load Order Hub to manage and validate.

assetPipeline.title: Learn the Asset Pipeline
assetPipeline.body: Textures use BC formats (BC1/BC3/BC7). Meshes are NIF files with Havok collision. BA2 archives hold compressed assets. Textures Hub and Guides Hub cover all of this.

gameStable.title: Keep Your Game Stable
gameStable.body: First identify your game version: OG (1.10.163), NG (1.10.980–984), or AE/1.11.x (1.11.191+). Then install the matching stack: F4SE + Address Library + X-Cell. Avoid deprecated AWKCR/DEF_UI — use ECO/NEO and FallUI instead. Use Creation Kit Hub for crash prevention monitoring.

buildPackage.title: Build & Package Your Mod
buildPackage.body: Use FO4 Mod Builder Hub to draft architecture, work in Workshop, build scripts in Devtools, and document in Scribe. Then go to Packaging & Release to create a BA2 and build your FOMOD installer.
